transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Tasha Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Maria Lopez (CISO, Hillside), Jon Peters (Head of ML), Priya Rao (Platform Engineer), Ellen Kim (Compliance)

Summary:
Hillside Health is scoping a 6-week pilot to validate Redwood's hosted + private options for PHI-adjacent workloads. Primary focus: security/compliance guardrails (SOC 2 / ISO), SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs, and benchmark targets (latency p95, throughput). Success criteria and timeline discussed; agreed to run a technical benchmark week of 2026-12-28. Redwood to provide security pack and benchmark spreadsheet.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency, throughput, quality)
- Workload sizing and expected token footprints
- Benchmarks and test harness
- Pilot timelines and gating criteria
- Security/compliance requirements: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM, data residency

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros. I'm Alex, AE. Samir is our SE, he'll run the benchmarks with you.
[00:18] Maria (Hillside CISO): Hi all, Maria here. We're the security owners. We want to make sure the pilot covers SOC 2 and SAML SSO integration, and that audit logs are searchable.
[00:30] Jon (Head of ML): Jon here; primary focus is throughput and latency on our summary-generation workload - about 300 tokens per response avg. We'll also test embeddings for search.
[00:44] Samir (Redwood SE): Great. High level, for pilots we usually do a 4-6 week scope: week1 baseline + access, week2 integration and small-scale tests, week3 full benchmark, week4 security review and tweaks, week5 ops handoff and runbook, week6 sign-off. We can compress if needed.
[01:05] Priya (Platform): On networking, we need VPC peering or private link; can't have customer data traversing public internet for PHI-related idents. Is private deployment an option for the pilot or do you support VPC peering with hosted endpoints?
[01:25] Alex: We support both. For pilots we often run hosted with VPC peering or dedicated pools. If you need on-prem, that's a longer path. For initial benchmark, VPC peering + private control plane is common.
[01:40] Ellen (Compliance): Also need to confirm data at rest encryption with KMS/HSM and key management options. We want to ensure logs are immutable and exportable for audits.
[01:53] Samir: We support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations for Private, and for hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS and customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. Audit logs are available via the Console and can stream to your SIEM. Note: sometimes the transcript will say K-V cash instead of KV cache, sorry for the auto-transcribe.
[02:20] Jon: On performance, our SLA for product is tight. For the pilot our success criteria: p95 latency <= 250ms for 256-token generation, sustained throughput 80-120 req/s, and embeddings at 200 req/s with <50ms p95. Are these targets reasonable?
[02:44] Samir: That's ambitious but doable on Dedicated or tuned hosted with batching/quantization profiles. Our recommendation: run an initial baseline at your expected token mix, then tune batching/windowing and quantization (int8/q4) if latency needs to be lowered. We'll provide kernel selection and CPU/GPU hints.
[03:05] Maria: SOC 2 type II is a hard requirement. Also want ISO27001 if possible, and a writeup for RBAC and SSO. We use SAML 2.0 with OneLogin. Can you provide SAML metadata and map groups for RBAC?
[03:23] Alex: Yes, we support SAML 2.0, OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning. We can send SAML metadata and sample attribute mappings. RBAC is configurable — roles, route-level permissions, and audit trails. We'll include a sample RBAC policy for your Compliance team to review.
[03:45] Priya: We also need to know retention windows for logs (additionally legal needs 7 years for some records). Can logs be exported to our S3 or SIEM and are they immutable?
[03:58] Samir: Logs can be streamed to your S3 bucket or SIEM; we keep immutable append-only audit logs with tamper evidence flags for Private deployments. For hosted we provide export and a retention config. We'll include export config examples.
[04:20] Jon: For benchmarks, what tooling do you use? We need reproducible harness and a spreadsheet to plug our traffic profile in.
[04:33] Samir: We'll share a benchmark spreadsheet with columns: request type, tokens in, tokens out, concurrency, expected qps, and target latency. We'll also provide a runbook and a k8s inference profile if you attempt on-prem. For hosted, we provide load agents and scripts.
[04:50] Maria: A few security questions: 1) do you have SOC 2 Type II report we can redline? 2) ISO27001 certificate? 3) penetration test summary? 4) incident response SLAs?
[05:05] Alex: We will share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certs, a redacted pentest summary, and our incident response playbook. For incident response we offer 24x7 on-call for Dedicated and Private customers under SLA.
[05:20] Ellen: For the pilot acceptance criteria, compliance needs: - SOC2 validated controls mapped to our risk register - SSO integration working end-to-end with test users - RBAC prevents data exfil from non-approved roles - Audit logs delivered to our SIEM and log retention confirmed
[05:38] Samir: We'll create a checklist mapping our controls to your risk register and mark pass/fail per test.
[05:46] Alex: To make this concrete, proposed pilot success criteria: 1) Security: SOC 2 Type II & ISO certs delivered; SAML SSO + SCIM provision working; RBAC roles defined and enforced; audit logs streaming to SIEM. 2) Performance: p95 latency <= 250ms for 256 tokens, throughput 80-120 rps on gen workload, embeddings at 200 rps. 3) Quality: sample prompts match current baseline on Rouge/ROUGE-like evals (we'll capture prompt set). 4) Ops: runbook and handoff complete.
[06:20] Jon: That looks good. Timeline?
[06:25] Samir: Proposed timeline: Week of 2026-12-21: security docs + test users + SAML metadata exchange. Week of 2026-12-28: baseline + benchmark runs (we'll run 1 full-day test and a 1-hour production-like test). Week of 2027-01-04: remediation/tuning and security review. Week of 2027-01-11: final sign-off. So ~3-4 weeks active work but we keep a 6-week window for scheduling.
[06:55] Priya: That works if we can get the SAML metadata and test dataset by 12/22 and run benchmarks 12/28. We also need an NDA addendum for PHI in pilot.
[07:05] Alex: We'll attach the standard pilot addendum and NDA.
[07:12] Maria: One more detail: can you show RBAC audit trails for object-level access (who viewed what)? We need to demonstrate per-user access logs.
[07:23] Samir: Yes, we log per-token request metadata, including user, route, model, and a hash of input (PII redaction optional). Those logs are queryable and exportable. For PHI we recommend redaction and client-side hashing of identifiable fields.
[07:42] Jon: On sizing: our estimate is 50k inference requests per day during peak pilot, average 300 tokens out, 50 tokens in. That maps to ~15M tokens/day. Any cost/throughput guidance?
[07:58] Alex: For that footprint, Dedicated or Reserved capacity will be more predictable cost-wise. We'll provide an estimate in the spreadsheet; in pilot we usually do a short reserved pool or burstable dedicated. Samir will put suggested instance sizes and GPU counts.
[08:15] Ellen: Regarding HIPAA: we're not fully HIPAA bound but some PHI-adjacent data will be in the pilot. We need to know Redwood's stance on BAA and whether pilot data can be covered.
[08:30] Alex: We can discuss BAA. For pilots we sometimes operate under a limited BAA or addendum; legal will follow up. We'll flag this as a gating item.
[08:42] Priya: For SSO mapping, we want group mappings to map to RBAC roles (e.g., group: ml-eng -> role: inference-engineer). Do you support attribute mapping?
[08:55] Samir: Yes, SAML attribute mapping and SCIM for groups. We'll share sample metadata and a small guide.
[09:05] Maria: Two more items: 1) Can audit logs be WORM (write once read many) for legal hold? 2) Is there an immutable chain of custody for logs?
[09:18] Samir: For Private deployments yes; for hosted we provide tamper-evident logs and integration with your SIEM to meet WORM and legal hold requirements. We'll include technical details.
[09:35] Alex: Great. Let's recap and next steps.
[09:40] Alex (Recap): Action items: Alex send security pack + SOC2/ISO certs + NDA addendum; Samir share benchmark spreadsheet and runbook; Priya provide dataset and SAML metadata; Maria/Ellen to review compliance pack. Schedule bench week of 12/28.
[09:58] Maria: Sounds good. We'll circulate internal stakeholders and confirm 12/22 deliverables.
[10:05] Jon: We'll also provide a short prompt set for quality eval by 12/22.
[10:12] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and attach docs.

End of call
